doctrine: Controls and retro-commissioning come BEFORE plant replacement: tune what exists, then size what remains
Demand measured baselines (12-mo interval or utility data) before crediting any modeled savings; modeled-only savings are provisional
Prefer measures the on-site operating staff can maintain; a BAS optimization nobody understands decays in 18 months
Typical scope: schedules, setpoints, economizer repair, sensor calibration, VFD additions on constant-volume systems, DCV where occupancy varies

Subscription-model RCx / monitoring-based commissioning (e.g. Parity): $0 owner capex but a recurring fee. Judge it on the ANNUAL NET — gross owner savings + risk-adjusted grid/PJM demand-response revenue − the fee — NOT on capitalized-fee-vs-utility-savings-alone (capitalizing a cancellable subscription at the exit cap makes the fee 'exceed' savings, an artifact). Its value is DR monetization + $0 capex + savings persistence (continuous commissioning stops loop drift), not first-order utility savings.
When a subscription is net-marginal without DR, present a ONE-TIME retro-commissioning alternative (a capex project, no perpetual fee) alongside it so the owner sees the structuring choice.

WSHP-loop towers built in the last ~5 years are prime RCx candidates (mis-tuned condenser loop / boiler staging / MAU schedules); ~1–2 yr payback typical, 100% owner-captured where the loop is gas-heated.
origination_prompts: Does the audit or PCA mention economizers, dampers, or actuators in fair/poor condition? RCx candidate.
Are HVAC schedules running 24/7 in the audit's operating description for a property with predictable occupancy?
Constant-speed pumps or fans older than 15 years with variable loads => VFD candidate.
feasibility_checks: Confirm BAS exists and is programmable (PCA systems description); pneumatic-only controls change the measure scope
Tenant disruption: RCx is low-disruption but schedule changes need property-management sign-off
Check Shovels for local controls contractors' permit activity as a market-availability signal
